    Delta Weight-And-Balance Outage Triggers Atlanta Ground Stop Days Before Thanksgiving

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Delta Air Lines flights bound for Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) were held at their departure airports on Sunday morning after an outage affected the carrier's weight-and-balance calculations.
    • According to recent reports, delta stated it was using "manual workarounds" while its teams worked to restore the automated system.
    • According to recent reports, according to the FAA's National Airspace System (NAS) status page, the ground stop on Sunday morning was imposed on Delta flights bound for Atlanta.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Delta Air Lines flights bound for Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) were held at their departure airports on Sunday morning after an outage affected the carrier's weight-and-balance calculations. The concern led the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to issue a ground stop at Delta's request, affecting hundreds of flights and causing mounting delays.

    According to recent reports, delta stated it was using "manual workarounds" while its teams worked to restore the automated system. While the ground stop was later downgraded to a ground delay program, the disruption came on the Sunday before Thanksgiving, with the holiday travel rush already underway.

    According to recent reports, according to the FAA's National Airspace System (NAS) status page, the ground stop on Sunday morning was imposed on Delta flights bound for Atlanta. It was initially scheduled to remain in place until at least 9:00 AM ET, but was downgraded to a ground delay program shortly after 8:40 AM. The change allowed flights to resume operating under restrictions, although delays are expected to continue as the carrier worked through its backlog.

    Sources indicate that FAA data highlighted inbound delays averaging 57 minutes, while flight tracking data shows that over 400 flights have been delayed at ATL, accounting for almost 20% of all inbound and outbound flights at the country's busiest airport. According to Atlanta News First, Delta passengers have also reported significant delays at airports including Newark, New York LaGuardia, Reagan National, Washington Dulles, Boston, Baltimore, Miami and Minneapolis.

    In a recent development, the issue affected Delta's Automated Load Instruction System (ALIS), which handles loading information used in aircraft weight-and-balance calculations. At the time of writing, Delta had not disclosed what caused Sunday's outage, or whether any flights had been canceled as a result. Simple Flying contacted the airline for comment and received the following statement:.

    "Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation. We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism.".

    In its statement, Delta stated its teams were working to restore automated weight-and-balance calculations for departing flights and that it was handling calculations manually. The airline added that it was working with air traffic control to "protect airport gates and tarmac areas from congestion" at ATL.

    In a recent development, weight-and-balance calculations are a critical part of airline operations and are typically handled by automated systems. Every flight needs a final load sheet before departure to confirm total weight and center of gravity after passengers, bags, cargo and fuel have been loaded. These figures are then used to calculate takeoff performance, including the speeds pilots need and the engine thrust required for departure.

    In a recent development, when the automated system fails, airlines must complete the calculations manually, adding time to the process for every flight. At a hub as large as Atlanta, slower departures mean aircraft remain at their gates longer, leaving fewer spaces available for arriving flights. Holding inbound Delta flights at their departure airports helps prevent aircraft from arriving in Atlanta without an available gate.

    Sources indicate that this can help limit congestion on the ground, but it also means delays can build up at airports where Delta aircraft are waiting to depart for Atlanta. Only last week, United Airlines suffered a similar weight-and-balance system outage that forced it to hold departures across its network. The disruption lasted more than 90 minutes and demonstrated how heavily airlines rely on automated systems to keep flights moving.

    Sources indicate that the disruption occurred during the opening weekend of the travel rush before Thanksgiving, which falls on Thursday, November 26. US carriers are projected to fly nearly 29 million passengers between November 20 and November 30, representing around 2.7 million per day. Airlines are also stepping up their Thanksgiving capacity year-on-year, offering 38,000 more daily seats than during the same period in 2025.

    According to recent reports, like all US carriers, Delta was significantly impacted by the recent nationwide ground stop on November 13 that lasted more than four hours. The stoppage followed a telecommunications failure within the FAA's system and affected flights nationwide. Delta struggled to recover its operations over the following days after aircraft and crews became displaced across its network, resulting in further delays and cancellations.

    Industry observers note that A judge said he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., which included a search of her Washington house last month.

    Sources indicate that judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search. Boasberg ordered the government to provide him by Friday what could be disclosed in the case. He pointed to how investigators are handling the “speech or debate” clause immunity that Omar has as a sitting member of Congress.

    “This is purely legal questions, interesting questions, about the privilege, the extent of the privilege and how it would apply,” Boasberg said.

    The Constitution includes an immunity for members of Congress for the “speech or debate” they engage in as part of their jobs.

    Boasberg also directed the government to propose redactions to the as-yet secret docket. While he mentioned next week’s expected disclosures would not include the 67-page document that investigators provided to justify the search, he left the door open to unsealing that down the road if the government closes the case or brings charges.

    Justice Department attorney Alessandra Serano argued against broad disclosures, calling it “very rare that a precharging, pre-indictment unsealing would happen.”.

    The high-profile nature of the investigation leaked into the courtroom Tuesday, as Boasberg cited statements by President Donald Trump and others about the investigation into Omar.

    “You have had administration officials, prominent ones, talking about the purpose of the investigation,” Boasberg remarked.

    Administration officials have accused Omar of committing immigration crimes for years, and Trump noted last month the DOJ was looking into Omar “strongly.” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on a recent podcast that investigators had served multiple search warrants and were investigating possible immigration fraud tied to when Omar entered the United States as a child.

    Separately, Boasberg stated he may concern rulings in the coming weeks unsealing portions of other court cases tied to the investigation, including one brought by Omar herself earlier this month seeking the return of the items seized in the search.

    In a recent development, the administration executed the search warrant in October, just a few weeks before the midterm elections. The timing of the search drew accusations of political bias from Democrats who claimed that the administration brought the case to sway the midterm elections.

    For years Trump has said he wanted criminal charges to be brought against his political foes, including Omar and others in Congress.

    #65497. Why JSX Just Bought New Pacific Airlines, The Strange, Failed 757 Startup

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1049 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Why JSX Just Bought New Pacific Airlines, The Strange, Failed 757 Startup

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Public charter air carrier JSX has just acquired New Pacific Airlines, and with this, New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights, with Embraer E145 aircraft.
    • If you’re not familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “huh?” If you are familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “WTF?” There’s a sneaky and logical explanation here, so let me explain.
    • JSX is a public charter air carrier, which operates a fleet of nearly 60 planes, most of which are Embraer E135s and E145s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Public charter air carrier JSX has just acquired New Pacific Airlines, and with this, New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights, with Embraer E145 aircraft.

    If you’re not familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “huh?” If you are familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “WTF?” There’s a sneaky and logical explanation here, so let me explain.

    Let’s start with a little context. JSX is a public charter air carrier, which operates a fleet of nearly 60 planes, most of which are Embraer E135s and E145s.

    It operates as a Part 135 operator, meaning it’s not technically an airline, as it’s using a loophole that allows it to not use standard TSA security screening, hire pilots with fewer than 1,500 hours, etc. Basically what’s happening is that one subsidiary sells the tickets, and then another subsidiary operates the flights, so it’s technically a “charter” (with 30 people who don’t know one another).

    Then there’s Upcoming Pacific Airlines, one of the strangest airline startups we’ve ever seen, and which I’ve covered extensively. The airline acquired some Boeing 757s, and the business strategy was to connect North America and Asia via Anchorage (ANC).

    The business model made zero sense in the first place, though there was some funding there, and they even invested in constructing a lounge in Anchorage, even though those flights never did happen. The airline did briefly fly from (ONT) to Nashville (BNA) — as one does — before ultimately going out of business.

    Industry observers note that that brings us to the news. New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with Embraer E145s that are leased from JSX, as reported by IshrionA. According to a Department of Transportation filing, the airline intends to resume flights with planes featuring 42 seats, which is higher than the 30-seat limit you’ll find on current JSX planes.

    Sources indicate that JSX acquires New Pacific Airlines.New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with ERJ 145 leased from JSX. pic.twitter.com/uMMS0J2fZy.

    Industry observers note that on the surface, this of course makes absolutely no sense. Upcoming Pacific Airlines was out of business, and the business model made no sense. So why would JSX buy an airline and then lease planes to it?

    In a recent development, long story short, this seems to be a play to acquire a cheap Part 121 certificate. A Part 121 operator is a organization that’s allowed to operate scheduled air transport… in other words, a “real” airline. As I mentioned above, JSX has historically been a Part 135 operator, and that explicitly means it’s not an airline. It’s a public charter air carrier, so it’s not a “real” airline.

    Going back a couple of years, we know that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was considering cracking down on carriers like JSX, since they definitely don’t operate within the spirit of the rules. That’s not to say that JSX did anything wrong, because by the letter of the law, they’re following it exactly. It’s just that the letter of the law makes no sense, and clearly doesn’t reflect the intent behind distinguishing between Part 121 and Part 135 operators.

    Industry observers note that under Trump, there was no scrutiny of this. However, with Democrats soon controlling both the House and Senate, I imagine JSX leaders may be worried that there could again be more scrutiny. If nothing else, buying a cheap Part 121 certificate is a good insurance policy, in case the government does crack down. After all, these can basically be “sold,” while acquiring one from scratch can be grueling process.

    According to recent reports, I wouldn’t assume that anything will really operate with Latest Pacific Airlines branding, or based on a New Pacific Airlines business model. Instead, I imagine the idea is that JSX will start dabbling in Part 121 operations, which is why these planes will have more seats (above the 30-seat cap that’s allowed), since that’s no longer a factor.

    Recent findings suggest that if the government were to crack down on Part 135 operators, JSX could move to Part 121 operations. However, they’d have to make lots of changes, from their pilot hiring, to the way passengers are screened.

    JSX has just bought Fresh Pacific, the airline with an absurd business model that went bankrupt. No, JSX isn’t inspired by the concept of flying Boeing 757s to Asia. Instead, this is clearly the cheapest way for JSX to acquire a Part 121 certificate, which would be required for the carrier to continue operations in the event that the government were to crack down on the Part 135 operator loophole.

    It’s going to be interesting to see how this evolves, both since JSX seems to have prepares to operate Part 121 operations in the near future, and also to see how JSX’s business model would evolve if the Part 135 concept were blocked.

    What do you make of this JSX Part 121 play?

I’ve read it four times, conscripted it as an airplane companion, and brought it to the beach. Yet its binding remains strong, its cover quite flexible, and its pages yellowing but intact. We no longer much refer to let alone read such 1941 bestsellers as Clifton Fadiman’s Reading I’ve Liked or Margaret Leech’s Reveille in Washington. But James Burnham, much like my strong and solid copy of his most famous book, endures.

    Burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation. The Managerial Revolution, anticipating as it did the ascension of technocrats, specialists, and the bureaucratic elite as a sort of ruling class, surely helped in that regard. Burnham remains read, despite no Burnhamite clique in academia or organized faction among movement conservatives dedicated to advancing his ideas. Kirkians, Straussians, and Randians exist. Why no James Burnham Preservation Society with an accompanying secret handshake?

    Daniel J. Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S. Meyer, is an American Spectator senior editor, visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution, and YouTuber @RightWingWilderness.

    On “The Complex Reputation of James Burnham”.

    #65493. Showers & Bars: The Onboard Spaces Only The Airbus A380 Offers

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1566 w)

    Showers & Bars: The Onboard Spaces Only The Airbus A380 Offers

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Airbus A380 Superjumbo is the world's only full two-decked passenger aircraft, and as such, it provides much more room for airlines to utilize for luxury spaces such as a bar, lounge, and showers.
    • Sources indicate that just having more space available for communal areas like bars, larger washrooms, and lounges doesn't mean that an aircraft actually will have more than its smaller predecessors.
    • Sources indicate that perhaps the only luxury element that the A380 can exclusively claim among scheduled passenger airliners today is showers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Airbus A380 Superjumbo is the world's only full two-decked passenger aircraft, and as such, it provides much more room for airlines to utilize for luxury spaces such as a bar, lounge, and showers. Still, a traveler from the past may be taken aback by how little luxury space the giant aircraft has. It is extremely rare in today's world for modern passenger airliners to have a significant amount of rest and recreation space, even though this was once the norm. In some ways, Emirates' configurations of the Superjumbo preserve a vestige of the past.

    Sources indicate that just having more space available for communal areas like bars, larger washrooms, and lounges doesn't mean that an aircraft actually will have more than its smaller predecessors. The Superjumbo is famous for its mostly Emirates configuration, having onboard lounges, bars, and showers. But this is almost a throwback to the past, with the industry moving from communal areas to privacy. As A380s age and receive their midlife refits, this trend towards privacy becomes clear even for the world's largest aircraft.

    Sources indicate that perhaps the only luxury element that the A380 can exclusively claim among scheduled passenger airliners today is showers. Only two airlines have installed showers for their premium guests, Emirates and Etihad. Emirates was the only airline to fit showers to its A380s from 2008 until 2014, when Etihad took delivery of its A380s. Both airlines fit the showers in the 'crown area' at the front of the upper deck, ahead of first class.

    It has been revealed that emirates has two Shower Spas and a lavatory for its 14-seat first-class cabin. Etihad has a first-class shower suite and a private shower within The Residence on its A380s. With Emirates, each passenger can expect five minutes of hot water, tracked by a digital timer, while 25-minute slots are booked with an onboard spa attendant. The shower rooms have heated floors. Emirates A380s configured without first class also lack showers.

    Recent findings suggest that etihad has two lavatories for nine-first class passengers, of which one has a shower, without a heated floor and half the size of Emirates'. The Residence is a three-room private apartment above first class. Some business jets have showers as an option, while some VIP and government airlines have them. Air Force One's VC-25 has a shower in the president's private executive suite​​​​​.

    Emirates is also famous for its lounge at the back of the upper deck, with a staffed bar and seating for first and business class passengers. Etihad calls its lounge (complete with sofas) The Lobby. But these two rival UAE carriers are not the only A380 operators to install lounges in their A380s. Qantas indicates its A380 "features a stylish onboard lounge for First and Business, a private upper deck for Business and Premium Economy, and a self-service snack bar in Economy.".

    Qatar Airways is known for its spacious bar and social lounge on the upper deck for first and business class passengers. Korean Air also has lounge areas on the upper deck. Historically, this included the Celestial Bar, although this was converted into a self-serve snack area. The spaces remain, but the dedicated bar service has largely been discontinued.

    Recent findings suggest that the A380 is not unique in offering bars, but it is notable for being able to accommodate full-size cocktail bars. Bars and lounges are somewhat common among premium mainline carriers. Virgin Atlantic states, "Depending on your aircraft, you might find The Loft, The Booth or The Bar." The Bar is found on its A330 and 787 aircraft. However, the trend is away from these luxuries, and the airline is phasing out its traditional onboard bars by 2028–2030 as part of a cabin overhaul.

    Sources indicate that etihad's The Residence is perhaps one of the most striking offerings only found on Airbus A380s. Eithad describes it as "An exclusive three-room suite in the sky, offering complete privacy, personalised service, and refined living from door to destination." Passengers can enjoy a fully private three-room suite with a lounge, bedroom, and en-suite bathroom. The airline provides a dedicated onboard team for The Residence customers.

    Service includes a private chauffeur, delivery of baggage directly to the destination (skip baggage claim in Abu Dhabi), a personal guide through the airport, and more. The cost of booking The Residence is reportedly from $11,000 to $25,000 one-way. While Etihad is purchasing the Airbus A350-1000, Boeing 787-9, and 777-9 twin-engined airliners, it is unclear when it prepares to retire its A380s. It recently reactivated the last stored A380, bringing its fleet to about nine.

    The pending retirement of A380s around the world does not mean the complete end of luxury communal space in aircraft like bars and lounges. That remarked, these spaces are clearly in decline (as is first class), and Emirates has suggested the showers will go when the A380s go. Qantas is bringing forward its retirement of its A380s and replacing them with A350-1000ULRs. The full bar service will be replaced by the much less opulent Wellbeing Zone.

    The Graf Zeppelin airship provided the world's first nonstop transatlantic passenger service. It had a kitchen, passenger lounge and dining room (the ship's only public space), and washrooms. The Hindenburg was the next-generation development of the Graf Zeppelin and had passenger space on two decks. It boasted a dining room, lounge (with a 356-lb Bluthner baby grand piano), a writing room, and port and starboard promenades. On the lower deck, it had a barroom and, most eye-catching for a hydrogen-filled airship, a smoking room.

    It has been revealed that as the world switched to airplanes away from airships, travel time across the Atlantic was cut from days to hours. The luxury space contracted, but didn't disappear. The Boeing 314 Clipper was one of the first transatlantic nonstop aircraft. Its luxury amenities were modeled after ocean liners and sleeper trains. It had separate passenger compartments, a 14-seat dining room, a lounge, and a convertible sleeping berth.

    Sources indicate that the Clipper offered separate men's and women's dressing rooms with sinks, mirrors, and towels, and even a shoe-polishing service. Following WWII, the Boeing 377 Stratocruiser was also a flying ocean liner, offering sleeping berths, separate men's and women's dressing rooms, a full galley, and a spiral staircase leading to a 14-seat lower-deck cocktail lounge. There are too many early aircraft to list here that came with lounges and bars.

    In a recent development, in the 1960s, as it designed the Boeing 747 Jumbo, Boeing expected supersonic long-range travel to be taken over by supersonic jets. It therefore designed the aircraft to be easily converted into a freighter. By raising the cockpit, Boeing allowed freighters to load oversized containers directly through an upward-hinged nose door. This created the upper deck and usable space behind the cockpit.

    It has been revealed that as this was the 1960s and 1970s, air travel was still expensive, predominantly upper-class, and luxurious. Boeing anticipated airlines using this 'leftover space' as a luxury lounge space for premium travelers. In the early days, airlines used it as a passenger lounge and bar. Pan Am fitted it with a 16-seat cocktail lounge and restaurant with sofas, swivel chairs, and tables, and experimented with a restaurant.

    Luxury philosophy (per Airships.net, etc.).

    Exclusive air travel, luxury hotel with lounges and smoking room (Hindenburg).

    Elite travel, dining rooms, sleeping berths.

    Spacious cabins, sleeper berths, lounges.

    Mass travel with lounges, bars, restaurants.

    Higher occupancy, dedicated premium seating.

    Personal space, privacy, premium cabins (lounges disappearing).

    Qantas made the themed Captain Cook Lounge, American installed the Captain's Deck First Class Lounge, while Braniff used it as a lounge with contemporary furniture and a distinctly 1970s aesthetic. American Airlines leaned into the 747 LuxuryLiner marketing for the early Jumbo. Not only did American install a lounge in the upper deck, but also a standing bar in the economy cabin on the main deck.

    The Airbus A380 offered unprecedented luxury in the skies in terms of overall space, room for features, and environmental cabin comfort. However, it did not represent a move to luxury social spaces. Instead, the A380 arguably sat at the intersection of two different eras. To some extent, what social spaces and seating density are not for Airbus to decide; that is for the airlines, driven by market demand.

    In the past, airlines heavily advertised social spaces like lounges, restaurants, and bars. But over time, the emphasis has moved to personal space, privacy, beds, and suites. Korean Air installed them, and then abandoned its Celestial Bar is one example of the shift happening in the A380's lifetime. Instead of communal spaces, Simple Flying's articles about modern business class cabins rolling out around the world are typically more concerned with privacy doors. The new luxury is a type of personal office cubicle.

    Sources indicate that if Emirates is right, and inflight showers disappear with the A380, the Superjumbo would mark a transitional moment. It arguably marks the final nail in the proverbial coffin for communal spaces on aircraft. Ironically, the much smaller Boeing 314 Clipper and Boeing 377 offered more luxury communal space than most of today's A380s. Something similar happened with the Boeing 747. Over time, the upper deck grew, but its use as a common lounge and bar space vanished.

Dwight Evans in a deep-blue district based in West Philadelphia.

Rick Scott, R-Fla., and looks to keep pushing for a bill he helped draft that aims to crack down on foreign surrogacy contracts. “We are at the moment selling American children to China, our No. 1 adversary,” Rogers stated, describing it as “deplorable.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, if you spend a lot at supermarkets and want to earn cash back, the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express is hard to beat. The card offers 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets and on select streaming subscriptions, which can add up fast for families and anyone with a few monthly subscriptions.

    In this post, I’ll cover the welcome offer, the bonus categories and how they work, the Disney streaming credit, and how this card compares to other options like the no annual fee Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express and the Citi Strata Premier® Card.

    Link: Learn more about the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express.

    Before I get into the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card review, here’s a quick look at the most important features and fees:.

    And here are my thoughts on the main pros and cons of the Blue Cash Preferred Card:.

    When applying for a credit card, obviously the welcome offer, the eligibility, and the fees, are major considerations, given that they can be the first factors that impact interest in a card. So along those lines, let’s take a look at those details for the Amex Blue Cash Preferred.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred is presently offering the following welcome bonus: You may be eligible for as high as $300 cash back after spending $3,000 in purchases on your upcoming Card in the first 6 months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Cash back is received as Reward Dollars, redeemable for statement credit or for other select options. Terms Apply.

    Sources indicate that that’s a solid bonus for a card at this price point, and the six month window gives you plenty of time to hit the spending requirement. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer.

    Amex cards tend to be fairly easy to get approved for if you have excellent credit. A few rules to know:.

    As you can see, this card is marketed as offering a bonus “as high as” a certain amount. The way this works, you can apply for the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card, and then find out your offer amount. Then you can decide whether you want to accept the offer or not. That’s an unconventional approach for a welcome offer. At least Amex has the “apply with confidence” feature, so there won’t be a hard pull unless you accept the offer.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred has a $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $95. (Rates & Fees). That puts it in line with other mid-range cards. No first year annual fee is a nice perk, as it lets you test the card and see how much value you’re getting before you commit to the ongoing fee.

    If you decide the card isn’t working for you after the first year, you can always downgrade to the no annual fee Blue Cash Everyday Card.

    You can add authorized users to the card at no extra cost, so that their spending can help you rack up rewards.

    Recent findings suggest that I wouldn’t recommend using the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card outside the U.S. or for purchases in foreign currencies. The 2.7% foreign transaction fee will eat into your rewards (Rates & Fees). There are plenty of other cards with no foreign transaction fees that are better suited for international spending.

    In a recent development, the Amex Blue Cash Preferred has some excellent bonus categories, especially if you spend a lot at U.S. supermarkets and on streaming. Below is a full breakdown.

    In a recent development, this is the headline feature of the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, and it’s the single best cash back rate for U.S. supermarket spending that I’m aware of. You earn 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets on up to $6,000 per year in purchases (then 1%). This is the only bonus category with an earning cap.

    To put that in perspective, if you spend $500 a month on U.S. supermarket spending, you’d earn $360 per year in cash back from this category alone. That more than covers the $95 annual fee.

    Note that supermarkets don’t include superstores, warehouse clubs (like Costco or Sam’s Club), or discount stores. If most of your grocery shopping happens at a traditional supermarket, this card is incredibly rewarding.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred also offers 6% cash back on select U.S. streaming subscriptions. The list of qualifying services is quite long and includes most of the major platforms: Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, ESPN+, HBO Max, Spotify, Apple TV, Apple Music, Amazon Music Unlimited, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV, Peacock, Sling TV, and many more.

    If you’re spending $50 to $100 a month across streaming services (which many households are these days), that 6% adds up nicely.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred offers 3% cash back on transit purchases, including taxis, ridesharing, parking, tolls, trains, and buses. If you commute by public transit or use rideshare services regularly, this is a solid bonus category.

    Industry observers note that with the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, you also earn 3% cash back at eligible U.S. gas stations, with no caps. Note that this doesn’t include gas purchased at superstores, supermarkets, or warehouse clubs that sell fuel.

    In a recent development, for purchases that don’t fall into the bonus categories, you earn 1% cash back. This is the one weak spot of the card. At just 1% on non-bonused spending, you’ll want to pair this card with something that earns a better return on everyday purchases (more on that below).

    With the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, you earn Reward Dollars that can be redeemed as statement credits, and there’s no minimum cash back balance required before you can redeem. It’s simple and straightforward, though it’s worth knowing that you can’t use cash back to pay your minimum payment due.

    As is the case for any credit card, it’s also crucial to consider the benefits and credits offered, if any. The Amex Blue Cash Preferred has a reasonable annual fee, so what are the benefits like? Well, they’re potentially pretty solid, and can help justify the annual fee….

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred offers up to $10 back per month ($120 per year) as a statement credit when you use your enrolled card to purchase a subscription, including a bundle subscription, on DisneyPlus.com, Hulu.com, or Stream.ESPN.com U.S. websites, with no minimum purchase requirement. Subscription is subject to auto-renewal. (Enrollment required).

    Another Amex Blue Cash Preferred benefit is access to Amex Presale Tickets® and Amex Reserved Tickets®, which can come in handy if you’re trying to score tickets to an in-demand concert or sporting event.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred also includes an introductory 0% APR offer that can give you some breathing room on purchases and balance transfers.

    Enjoy 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 12 months from the date of account opening. After that, your APR will be a variable APR of 19.74% - 28.74%.

    This could be helpful if you need to transfer an existing credit card balance and have some time to pay it off before interest kicks in, or if you need some extra time to pay off a big upcoming purchase. Just make sure you pay off your balance in full before the intro period ends, or you’ll be on the hook for interest after all.

    Sources indicate that one benefit that doesn’t get enough attention is the Amex Offers program. This gives you access to targeted deals with a variety of retailers, just by registering your card and making an eligible purchase.

    According to recent reports, different Amex cards get different offers, so having multiple Amex cards in your wallet means more chances to save. Across my Amex cards, this program saves me hundreds of dollars per year.

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card has fewer travel protections than more premium Amex cards, but it does come with coverage to protect your rental car when you charge the rental to this card. The coverage applies for eligible damage or theft, and it’s secondary, so it kicks in after your own car insurance. There are some exclusions, and it doesn’t include liability coverage, so check your card benefits guide for the full details.

    Industry observers note that I tend to lean toward points-earning cards for my own spending, but I totally get why a lot of people prefer cash back. It’s simple, flexible, and you can spend it however you want, including on travel. For that crowd, the Blue Cash Preferred is one of the best options out there.

    If you’re someone who is looking to earn cash back and spends a lot at supermarkets, then the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card is an exceptional choice, in my opinion — 6% cash back will add up quickly.

    The 6% cash back on streaming, and 3% cash back on transit and gas stations, will add up quickly as well, and up to $120 Disney streaming credit could be worth more than the annual fee.

    However, this isn’t the card I would be using for your everyday spending, as you’d only earn 1% cash back in the categories that aren’t eligible for bonuses. So I’d acquire this card specifically with the intent of using it in the categories offering bonuses.

    So, let’s take a look at what other cards you should potentially be considering.

    If you like the idea of an Amex cash back card but aren’t sure about paying an annual fee, the Blue Cash Everyday Card from American Express (learn more) is the no annual fee alternative where you can earn as high as $200 cash back after spending $2,000 in purchases on your new Card in the first six months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Cash back is received as Reward Dollars, redeemable for statement credit or for other select options. Terms Apply.

    Here’s how the two Blue Cash cards compare:.

    In my opinion, the Blue Cash Preferred is well worth the annual fee if you spend a meaningful amount at supermarkets. The jump from 3% to 6% on U.S. supermarkets adds up fast. If you spend $500 a month at supermarkets, that extra 3% earns you $180 more per year, which nearly doubles the annual fee.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Cash Everyday does have one unique advantage: 3% cash back on U.S. online retail purchases, which the Preferred doesn’t offer. If you do a lot of online shopping and less grocery shopping, the Everyday could actually come out ahead.

    The good news is that you can always start with the Blue Cash Preferred and downgrade to the Blue Cash Everyday after the first year if the math doesn’t work out.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re just looking for the simplest cash back credit card, it’s tough to go wrong with the Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more). The card offers 1% cash back when you make a purchase, and 1% cash back when you pay for that purchase, for a total of 2% back on every purchase. That’s a solid return on everyday spending, and you don’t have to keep track of any bonus spending categories.

    It has been revealed that if you’re deciding between the Blue Cash Preferred and a mid-range card from another issuer, the $95 annual fee Citi Strata Premier Card (learn more) is worth considering. These two cards serve pretty different purposes, but they’re at the same price point:.

    The Blue Cash Preferred wins on supermarkets and streaming, hands down. If those are your biggest spending categories, the Blue Cash Preferred is the better card.

    Industry observers note that the Strata Premier is the more well-rounded card overall. It earns 3x points across five major categories (dining, gas, supermarkets, airfare, hotels), has no foreign transaction fees, and its ThankYou points can be transferred to airline and hotel partners for potentially much more than face value. If you travel or eat out a lot, the Strata Premier likely comes out ahead.

    In a recent development, one final card worth considering alongside the Blue Cash Preferred Card is the American Express® Gold Card (learn more). It has a significantly higher annual fee, but it’s unbeatable for earning rewards at U.S. supermarkets — you’ll earn transferable Membership Rewards points too, rather than cash back.

    Here’s a look at how they compare:.

    The Blue Cash Preferred is the best cash back card for supermarket spending, and it’s not particularly close. If groceries and streaming are a substantial part of your monthly budget, this card can deliver serious returns, especially with the 6% rate on both categories plus the Disney streaming credit.

    It has been revealed that the annual fee pays for itself quickly if you’re spending even a moderate amount at supermarkets. Pair it with a card like the Citi Double Cash for your non-bonused spending, and you’ve got a strong cash back setup.

    Industry observers note that just keep in mind that the 1% rate on everyday purchases means this card works best as a specialist, not your only card. Use it where it shines, and let a flat-rate card handle the rest.

    Breaking: LATAM Airlines unveils latest A321XLR cabins with eye on US expansion

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (332 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.
    • After opening dozens of latest transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027.
    • LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.

    After opening dozens of latest transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027. The airline has yet to say which routes the XLRs will fly, but executives have previously outlined opportunities to connect the U.S. and South America.

    LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats. Business class will feature 12 lie-flat suites supplied by Thompson Aero Seating in a 1-1 layout with privacy doors.

    The suites include 19-inch personal entertainment screens, Bluetooth connectivity and in-seat charging options.

    Economy features 13-inch screens at each of the 126 seats, which are supplied by Recaro, plus Bluetooth connectivity and USB-C outlets. The cabin includes 36 extra-legroom seats.

    “The Airbus A321XLR allows us to take our value proposition to the next level and elevate the travel experience for our passengers,” remarked Paulo Miranda, the chief customer officer of LATAM, in a statement. He described the interior, which features red, orange and blue hues, as “inspired by South America.”.

    LATAM executives have stated it could fly the XLR on routes into the U.S. from its hub at Jorge Chavez International Airport (LIM) in Lima. However, those prepares were called into question in May over the addition of a "connection fee" at LIM.

    The airline and Delta serve six U.S. destinations from LIM: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Orlando International Airport (MCO) and, since January 2026, Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).

    LATAM did not comment on specific route aims for the XLR.

    It has been revealed that the XLR is the second latest airplane type for LATAM in as many years. The airline took delivery of its first Embraer E195-E2 in October. It will use the small jet to expand its feeder network in Brazil and support additional long-haul, intercontinental flying.

    #65489. Latest Update: The American Genius of Madden

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (866 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: The American Genius of Madden

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (866 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Russell’s Madden, as its story of the Oakland Raiders football coach John Madden shifts between semidocumentary and biopic.
    • The key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football.
    • Sources indicate that madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hang on at the start of David O. Russell’s Madden, as its story of the Oakland Raiders football coach John Madden shifts between semidocumentary and biopic. Russell’s uneven, sketchy narrative steadily turns into a probing human comedy. It’s also a slyly monumental tale of American genius found in an Everyman’s commonplace ambition.

    The key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football. Cage enters the mindset of a sports fanatic who is also an artist, devising plays and strategies that, considering his size and vision, earn him the nickname “Buddha.” But this is not one of those freak-outs that Cage is known for; he seems to transform himself into John Candy — broad-beamed with a tuft of blond hair and a convincing smile. Cage commits to this genial eccentric who, despite his unreachable idiosyncrasy, is harmless, lovable yet tough — an authentic, original American.

    Sources indicate that madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend. This thick-and-thin Laurel-and-Hardy pair sustain an unlikely partnership. It’s one of the most remarkable depictions of brotherhood in movies — a friendship that persists over temperamental tensions, even after Madden leaves the team and pursues media entrepreneurship to sustain his love of the sport. Madden the broadcaster converts his playbook ingenuity and follows his father’s advice: “Get away with doing what you love for as long as you possibly can.”.

    It has been revealed that russell redeems himself with the oddest-yet-normal collection of American eccentrics. Acting on the edge of parody, Cage and Bale, with their uncanny sincerity, reward Russell’s interest in quirkiness. (Madden hears Davis’s voice in his head.) The fascinating scoundrels of Russell’s terrific American Hustle were preoccupied with manipulating one another. Here, friendship, comradeship, teamwork, and family complications are genuinely recognizable. Scenes that emulate a documentary approach — Madden’s wife Virginia (gung ho comedienne Kathryn Hahn) rivals Jennifer Lawrence’s volatility when speaking directly to the camera — satirize realism to fulfill the non-cynical view of national character that Russell fumbled in the bohemian sojourn of Amsterdam. No wonder De Niro is left out of this particular silver-lined playbook.

    Nicolas Cage (John Madden) in Madden.

    Chuck Zlotnick/Amazon MGM Studios.

    Industry observers note that the patchwork of styles in Madden suggests that Russell investigates American eccentricity as he goes along, finding his way back to the coast-to-coast realness that made his Flirting with Disaster so exhilarating (as in Madden’s surreal, unapologetic pitch for the unique holiday dish the Turducken). Russell adopts Madden’s football-analysis style, such as on-screen telestrator vectors, to humorously examine Madden’s own career shifts and twists of personality (Madden instructing his players, or meeting colleagues Pat Summerall, Howard Cosell, and Bob Costas).

    A dull-witted filmmaker, say James Cameron, would choose an “immersive” style for a movie concerned with the gestalt of football. But Russell’s film is also about the phenomenon of a sport that becomes a vanguard of technology and culture. Madden is pursued by Trip Hawkins (John Mulaney), founder of video game organization EA (Electronic Arts), who wants to translate Madden’s football theories for a fresh generation of at-home fans and gamers. Hawkins’s proposal is scored to Beethoven’s Ninth — another example of Russell’s wit, matching the film’s eclectic score from Barry White and Talking Heads to N.W.A. (“You don’t want to know what that means,” Davis states to Madden.).

    Through Madden and Hawkins’s acumen, Russell treats the discovery of a upcoming world as an aftereffect of folk intelligence and ingenuity. Genius is kidded when Hawkins’s team of four-eyed computer nerds demonstrate jock potential after applying Madden’s plays to their algorithms. It’s a sweet way of conveying the phenomenon that would turn EA’s Madden NFL video game franchise into a $4 billion enterprise (some estimates raise that into double digits), with annual compensation going to the Madden family estate.

    More notable, Russell (who co-wrote the script with Cambron Clark) sees Madden as a visionary who proudly summarizes TV sportscasting as “They state the obvious, which is f***ing boring.” My only complaint is that Robert Richardson’s photography tends toward frowzy (perhaps deliberately aping TV docs), not as splendid as Oliver Stone’s Any Given Sunday — the greatest football movie ever made.

    Madden itself shares biopic sensibility with John Ford’s The Wings of Eagles, respectfully eschewing its subject’s mortality for an optimistic appreciation of a man’s potential. It is unique to American character and the experience of competition and dreams of the NFL Hall of Fame that Madden shared with Al Davis. Russell’s tribute comes complete with a motto: “You make people feel good and alive and good to be American, and I’m not standing in the way of that.” Thus Russell proves his own resilience and the achievement of a new folkloric genre struggling to emerge.

    Armond White is National Review’s culture critic and the author of Newly introduced Position: The Prince Chronicles and Make Spielberg Great Again: The Steven Spielberg Chronicles.

    On “The American Genius of Madden”.

    #65486. Zinke PAC gave to family foundation he was investigated for

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1247 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Zinke PAC gave to family foundation he was investigated for

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1247 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025.
    • In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep.
    • Recent findings suggest that the gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke gave $200,000 in campaign cash to a family foundation headed by his wife that was once at the center of a federal investigation and an ethics scandal that led him to resign as Interior secretary in 2019.

    Recent findings suggest that the gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug. 31 from Zinke’s leadership political action committee to the nonprofit Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation, campaign finance records show. The donation is more than the foundation has reported receiving in any year since it was founded nearly two decades ago.

    Zinke’s wife, son, and sister currently serve on its board of directors, according to the foundation’s annual filing with the state of Montana.

    Industry observers note that in a brief interview, Zinke denied that any portion of the money transferred to the foundation will directly benefit him or any of his family members who sit on the board of directors. “No, no, never," he stated when asked if any family members will draw a salary from the gift.

    The money will instead go to building a storage barn and kid’s sledding park on the property controlled by the foundation, Zinke stated.

    None of the records indicate Zinke violated the law or directly benefited from the gift to his foundation.

    “While it's not uncommon for a politician to transfer leftover money from a political war chest to charity, it is pretty rare for a politician to transfer leftover political funds to a charity that they or a relative controls,” remarked Michael Beckel, director of money in politics reform at Issue One, a bipartisan group that seeks to reduce influence of money in politics.

    Instead, outgoing members typically transfer remaining campaign cash to local party committees or candidates, Beckel added.

    Ethics experts say Zinke’s move highlights ongoing concerns over the broad latitude campaign finance law gives leadership PACs in how they spend money.

    “I definitely think it is something to be concerned about,” said Stuart McPhail, director of campaign finance litigation at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit watchdog.

    “Leadership PACs are really nothing more than personal slush funds under today's rules,” he noted, noting that unlike regular campaign committees, member leadership PACs are not prohibited from donating to charities or organizations that could directly benefit the member or relative.

    Recent findings suggest that zinke, a former Navy SEAL who commanded special forces during the Iraq War, converted his traditional campaign committee to a leadership PAC — Commander Zinke Leadership Fund — in March 2026, shortly after announcing he would not run for reelection. It last reported having $1.4 million cash on hand in October of this year.

    It marks the second time one of Zinke’s political committees made a payment to the organization. In 2019, the committee Zinke ran during his earlier years in Congress — he served one term in the House before being tapped as Trump’s first-term Interior secretary — gave over $11,000 to the foundation before winding down operations.

    According to recent reports, the Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation was founded by Zinke and his wife in 2007 in his hometown of Whitefish, Mont., with plans to provide winter recreational activities for children. Its latest tax filing reports revenue of $15,000 and roughly equal expenses in 2024 for snow plowing and park maintenance.

    Zinke’s dealings with the organization were the subject of an ongoing inspector general investigation when he resigned as Interior secretary in January 2019.

    Investigators ultimately did not find that Zinke violated conflict-of-interest laws, but they concluded that he failed to comply with federal ethics obligations and “misused his official position in violation of federal regulations.” The Justice Department declined to prosecute Zinke.

    Sources indicate that zinke stepped down from the foundation in 2017, shortly after his Senate confirmation. But investigators found that he continued to represent the organization in negotiations with the developers of a commercial project adjacent to the foundation’s land and lied to an ethics agent about his involvement in the project.

    The project’s investors included David Lesar, then-chairman of oil services company Halliburton.

    Another Zinke-tied leadership PAC has previously raised eyebrows in Washington.

    According to recent reports, supporting Electing American Leaders PAC — known as SEAL PAC — where Zinke serves as chairman, has been marred by accusations that it funneled money to political consultants instead of candidates. A 2022 CQ Roll Call analysis found that 87 percent of the PAC’s spending went to operating expenses.

    The PAC also made recurring monthly payments to a tech giant registered to Zinke’s son, Wolfgang Zinke, and based at a Zinke family-owned home in Whitefish.

    Industry observers note that SEAL PAC’s executive director, Rob Catron, maintained that the payments constitute a consulting fee to Wolfgang Zinke for management of the PAC website, among other tasks. “He earns every penny of it,” Catron noted.

    Since May 2022, the PAC has given roughly $270,000 to Wolfgang Zinke’s firm, FG Solutions, for mailing and printing, records show — more than any individual candidate or committee supported by the PAC. The company also received $5,000 from a related super PAC, SEAL PAC USA, which can solicit unlimited contributions for independent expenditures but can’t donate directly to candidates.

    Montana corporate records show Wolfgang Zinke founded FG Solutions – which says it provides services including “personal assistant and any lawful purpose” – just 10 days before it received its first payment from the PAC in 2022.

    Catron defended how the PAC spends money on veterans running for the House, arguing that it takes money to raise money.

    “We raise a lion’s share of our funding through national direct mail fundraising, which is very expensive to do,” he said, citing the PAC’s use of a national text message fundraising campaign as a major expense.

    SEAL PAC raised about $9.6 million this election cycle, distributing about $1.1 million to GOP lawmakers and candidates, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Most of the committee's funds went to operating expenses, including over $3 million paid to Direct Support Services, a Washington-based vendor, for direct mail postage.

    Zinke’s not the only lawmaker to face scrutiny over how they spent surplus campaign cash in recent years.

    It has been revealed that in 2023, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., set off alarm bells for transferring $200,000 from his campaign committee to The Sanders Institute, a nonprofit founded by his wife and stepson, following a $350,000 donation from his 2020 presidential campaign coffers.

    The organization briefly shut down during Sanders’ presidential run in 2019 to avoid the appearance of impropriety.

    Sanders’ stepson, David Driscoll — a former executive at Nike and snowboard manufacturer Burton — is listed on the think tank’s website as its executive director, drawing a six-figure annual salary according to tax filings.

    It’s unusual, though not unheard of, for campaign committees to pay family members of the candidate for bona fide work.

    “If [Wolfgang Zinke] is actually performing this work, he’s qualified to do it, and this is his typical market rate for this kind of contract, then it would be permissible, even if this was a campaign account,” McPhail said about SEAL PAC's payments.

    But the payments could present a legal “gray area” over whether personal-use restrictions apply to certain PACs, according to McPhail.

    #65485. Why Boeing Built The 737 MAX With The Ability To Take Off Overweight, Even Though It Can't Legally & Operationally

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1531 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Boeing Built The 737 MAX With The Ability To Take Off Overweight, Even Though It Can't Legally & Operationally

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as with all other modern narrowbody aircraft, the Boeing 737 MAX offers a taxi allowance between its Maximum Takeoff Weight and its Maximum Taxi Weight.
    • It has been revealed that since the type first entered service in the 1960s, the margin on the 737 has been decreasing over time and reached a new record low in October 2026, when the FAA certified the MAX 10.
    • The vast majority of missions do not require Boeing 737s to operate at their maximum fuel capacities.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that as with all other modern narrowbody aircraft, the Boeing 737 MAX offers a taxi allowance between its Maximum Takeoff Weight and its Maximum Taxi Weight. This is related to ensuring the aircraft can actually take off with its maximum fuel capacity (by weight) in edge cases, as well as being related to safety margins.

    It has been revealed that since the type first entered service in the 1960s, the margin on the 737 has been decreasing over time and reached a new record low in October 2026, when the FAA certified the MAX 10. The taxi allowance is not particularly important, and when it comes to adding fuel capacity, it is only relevant in a small minority of cases.

    The vast majority of missions do not require Boeing 737s to operate at their maximum fuel capacities. That said, to some extent, the declining margins can be seen as another example of upgraded generations of 737s being constrained by an aging 1960s design. Here is what to know about why the 737 can be loaded heavier at pushback than at takeoff.

    Recent findings suggest that boeing has engineered its popular 737 MAX to support a ground weight higher than its Maximum Takeoff Weight mostly for operational flexibility, structural safety margins, and regulatory certification. For the purposes of this article's headline, Boeing certifies a higher Maximum Taxi Weight of around 500 lbs (around 227 kg) over its MTOW.

    Industry observers note that this allows airlines to load extra 'taxi fuel' at the gate without the need to sacrifice passengers or cargo. While only a small percentage of its overall fuel volume and aircraft weight, airliners do consume a measurable amount of fuel before they even take off. The APU, starting the engines, and ground taxiing all consume fuel and burn off the aircraft's excess weight before it commences its takeoff roll.

    A Boeing MAX or A320neo typically consumes 300 to 650 lb (135 to 295 kg) of fuel on a normal departure between refueling and the takeoff roll. During periods of heavy congestion, ground holds, or winter de-icing, this can be as much as 1,000+ lbs (450+ kg). A MAX 8 has a total fuel capacity of 46,063 lb (20,894 kg) of fuel.

    In a recent development, the pre-takeoff consumption represents around 0.7% to 1.4% of its total fuel volume. That said, they are typically not fully fueled. In these cases, the amount of onboard fuel burned before the take-off roll can be as much as 2% to 4% for a typical two- to three-hour flight.

    As a general rule, aircraft are routinely built to be able to be considerably more capable than what their sticker certifications suggest. To meet the strict FAA and EASA airworthiness standards, aircraft airframes are required to be built with substantial structural and aerodynamic safety margins.

    It has been revealed that aircraft are designed to survive hard landings, strong gusts, and minimum climb gradients during a single-engine failure. Yet another reason is that Boeing (and other airplane manufacturers) often design aircraft with greater structural capability than required for their standard operating configuration.

    In a recent development, this allows their aircraft to be certified and sold with different maximum take-off weight (MTOW) variants. For example, the A321neo family comes with multiple certified weight variants including 89, 90.5, 93.5, and 97 (A321LR) tonnes. The heavier A321XLR is more extensively modified.

    This means that an airline can purchase an A321neo certified at 89 tonnes when the same base aircraft family offers higher certified weight variants. The main advantage of operating an 89-tonne certified aircraft is to reduce weight-based airport and air navigation fees. It doesn't necessarily have a lower empty weight or dry operating weight compared with a 93.5-tonne aircraft.

    The Boeing 737 MAX's taxi allowance has actually decreased relative to its predecessor, the Boeing 737 Next Generation (NG). The MAX family inherited the 737NG certification baseline. Boeing opted to keep the 500 lb taxi allowance that the older NG came with and chose not to recertify it for a larger ground-maneuvering margin.

    In fact, Boeing has retained the 500 lb margin across all its generations and variants of the 737 from the 1960s 737-100 Original to the new MAX 10. However, the MTOW of these aircraft has not remained static. Over time, the MTOW has grown, squeezing the margin more and more.

    Percentage above MTOW (per Boeing).

    0.71% (A220-100), 0.68% (A220-300).

    0.53% (A320neo HGW), 0.40% (A321neo).

    0.28% (MAX 7), 0.27% (MAX 8), 0.26% (MAX 9), 0.25% (MAX 10).

    Recent findings suggest that the original 737-100 was built with a standard MTOW of 97,800 lb (44,361 kg) and an MTW (ramp) of 98,300 lb (44,588 kg). This was a margin of around 0.51% in the initially certified version (around 0.39% with the more popular 737-200). It is not possible to list all the subvariants of each generation here, but MTOW went up, and the margin went down.

    The taxi allowance of 500 lbs remained constant. The 737-400 Classic had a basic MTOW of 138,500 lb (62,823 kg) and a ramp weight of 139,000 lb (63,049 kg), or around 0.36%. The popular 737-800 (NG) came with an MTOW of 155,500 lb (70,534 kg) and an MTW (ramp) of 156,000 lb (70,760 kg), or a margin of 0.32%.

    The MAX family comes with four basic variants and one subvariant with differing MTOWs, while the taxi allowance remains constant. All four MAX variants are (finally) all certified. The shortened MAX 7 (also includes the BBJ MAX 7) has an MTOW of 177,000 lb (80,286 kg) and a ramp weight of 177,500 lb (80,513 kg).

    Being the lightest MAX variant, it offers a taxi allowance margin of 28%, the highest of the family. Next is the popular MAX 8 with a baseline MTOW of 181,200 lb (82,191 kg) and ramp weight of 181,700 lb (82,418 kg). Here, the margin remains at 0.28% due to rounding. The heavier BBJ MAX 8 falls to 0.27%.

    The high-density 737-8-200 (popular with low-cost airlines like Ryanair) has the same MTOW and ramp weights as the MAX 8. Unlike the A321XLR, it has more doors as the main modification, not heavier tanks. The margin remains 0.28%.

    The stretched MAX 9 is certified for an MTOW of 194,700 lb (88,314 kg) and a ramp weight of 195,200 lb (88,541 kg), causing the margin to fall to 0.26%. Finally, the extra-stretched MAX 10 pushes the margin to the family's lowest at just 0.25%. Its MTOW is 197,900 lb (89,766 kg) and ramp weight is 198,400 lb (89,992 kg), making it the heaviest.

    Industry observers note that it would be wrong to think of the MAX as being special with the weight margin or Boeing being some sort of over-engineering designer. Almost the opposite is true of modern narrowbody aircraft. ​​​​​​​With a taxi allowance of 500 lb (227 kg), Boeing gives a margin of around 0.27% above the MTOW.

    The main rival, the A320neo, has a taxi allowance of 882 lbs (400 kg) or a margin of around 0.51%. The margin is a little smaller on the A321neo, at around 0.43%, but still significantly more than the MAX 8 and MAX 9. These margins are also greater on the Airbus A220 and Embraer E-Jet E2.

    Industry observers note that ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​The A220 offers a much greater taxi allowance of 1,000 lbs (454 kg) despite being a much smaller aircraft. This is a margin of around 0.68%. The E-Jet E2 has a smaller absolute taxi allowance, 441 lbs (200 kg). However, these regional Embraer aircraft are also much smaller, and so the margin above MTOW is 0.33%, placing it ahead of the MAX.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, the MAX's erstwhile Chinese competitor, the COMAC C919, offers an 882 lb (400 kg) allowance and a margin of around 0.53%. The pre-sanctioned Russian MC-21 was to offer an allowance of 441 lbs (200 kg) or 0.25%. This made the MC-21 similar to the MAX.

    Continuously updating the 1960s-era Boeing 737 has plenty of challenges. One of the biggest recurring issues is its short landing gear, making it difficult to accommodate modern large-diameter engines under the wings. This led to the infamous MCAS software and the MAX crashes in 2017 and 2018.

    It has been revealed that other complications include the comparatively heavy aluminum airframe and narrow cabin (making it extra squishy in economy). The shrinking taxi margin is regarded as a minor operational nuisance on edge-case missions, rather than a major problem. Both Airbus and Boeing are starting work on their clean-sheet narrowbody replacements expected to debut in the mid-to-late 2030s.

    Industry observers note that efforts are in their early stages, and few details have been released; Boeing is considered behind Airbus in the design and development cycle. These aircraft are targeting a 20–25% lower fuel burn. They are expected to make use of thermoplastic composites, next-generation engines, perhaps folding wingtips, and other improvements.

    Sources indicate that it is reasonable to assume they will be designed with room for future growth. It would also be reasonable to assume Boeing would take the opportunity to boost the taxi allowance margin to around 0.5% to 0.7%, in line with industry norms.

    Amex Blue Cash Everyday Review: A No Annual Fee Card With Solid Bonus Categories
